title: Your First Universal Trip: Start Here
h1: Planning a First Trip to Universal
metaDescription: Orlando or Hollywood, how many days, the ticket decision that catches everybody, the height wall, and whether Express Pass is really a hotel decision.
summary: The five decisions that shape a first Universal trip, in the order you have to make them: which resort, how many days, which ticket, which hotel, and whether your shortest rider clears the heights that matter.
intro: Universal is a different planning problem from Disney, and most first-timers arrive with the wrong instincts. There is no sixty-day dining scramble, no morning alarm to book rides, and far less that has to be decided months out. What there is instead is a small number of decisions that are expensive to get wrong and impossible to fix once you are there.

Two of them happen before you buy anything. The first is the ticket: a base ticket admits you to one park per day, and the Hogwarts Express will not board one. The second is the hotel: Universal Express Pass is included with three of Universal Orlando's ten hotels and not with the other seven, and on a busy trip for a family of four the premium on those three can come in under what buying Express separately would cost.

The third decision is the one that actually ruins trips, and it is about height. Universal's thrill tier starts where Disney's tops out — 48, 51, 52 and 54 inches are ordinary numbers here. A family whose youngest child is under 40 inches will find far more to do at Magic Kingdom than at Islands of Adventure, and pretending otherwise is how a week goes wrong. Measure everybody before you book.

The reward for getting those three right is a resort that is, ride for ride, the most rewarding in the country for anyone tall enough and inclined to be thrown around. Universal Orlando is now three parks and genuinely needs three to four days. Universal Studios Hollywood is one park, one day, and is a completely different proposition that happens to share a name.
keyPoints: Universal Orlando is three parks and needs three to four days. Universal Studios Hollywood is one park and one day.
The Hogwarts Express requires a park-to-park ticket in both directions, and no upgrade is sold at the platform.
Express Pass is included at three Universal Orlando hotels and not at the other seven. Do that arithmetic before you book a room.
Every on-site Universal Orlando hotel gets Early Park Admission, which is a different and much cheaper benefit than Express.
The heights are higher than at Disney. Measure your shortest rider before you commit to a park, let alone a trip.
Download the Universal app and set up the account and payment method before you arrive. The in-park network is congested.
Single rider lines run at twelve attractions across the two original Orlando parks and cost nothing. For two adults they cover most of what Express buys.

sections.heading: Universal Orlando or Universal Studios Hollywood?
body: These are not two versions of the same thing. Universal Orlando is a three-park destination with a hotel system, a walkable core and enough ride capacity to fill four days. Universal Studios Hollywood is a single park on a genuine working studio backlot in Los Angeles, built into a hillside, doable in one day, and built around a tram tour nothing else replicates.

Orlando is bigger in every direction — three parks, more rides, longer versions of several attractions Hollywood also has, and a hotel tier that includes Express Pass. Hollywood has the Studio Tour, which Orlando cannot replicate, and it fits into a Los Angeles trip rather than requiring one. If you will only ever visit one, visit Orlando. If you live in Southern California, Hollywood is a very good day out and does not need a hotel.

The intensity difference is the other thing to weigh. Universal's headliners skew toward high-motion simulators and serious roller coasters at both resorts, and the height requirements are correspondingly strict. Orlando has more for a family with small children than Hollywood does, mostly because it has more of everything, but neither park is where a preschooler has the best day of their life.

Getting there differs too. Orlando International is about twenty minutes from Universal Orlando, closer than it is to Walt Disney World, and Universal runs no free airport shuttle — a rental car, a rideshare or a paid shuttle are the options. For Hollywood, Burbank is closest and easiest, and the Metro B Line stops at Universal City with a free shuttle up the hill, which makes it the rare Los Angeles attraction genuinely reachable without a car.

sections.heading: How many days you actually need
body: Three park days is the honest minimum at Universal Orlando now that Epic Universe exists. Two covers the two original parks at a rush and leaves Epic Universe out entirely. Four lets you repeat the headliners, which at Universal is more of the point than it is elsewhere — VelociCoaster and Revenge of the Mummy reward second and third rides in a way a Disney dark ride does not.

The three parks are not equal in day length. Universal Studios Florida and Epic Universe each fill a day comfortably. Islands of Adventure is the one that repays more than a day if your party can ride everything in it, both because the ride list is the strongest at the resort and because Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure has to be done at rope drop or at close, which is hard to fit into a shared day.

Epic Universe wants its own day or days. It is on a separate campus a short drive south, reached by resort shuttle bus, car or rideshare, and that transfer needs building into both ends of the day. Trying to hop in or out of it mid-afternoon burns close to an hour and most people who do it once do not do it twice.

For Hollywood, one day is genuinely enough. A second only makes sense if the first was cut short. The park is compact and the constraint is vertical rather than horizontal: the Upper Lot and Lower Lot are joined by a long series of escalators, and planning the day to minimise round trips between them matters more than anything else you can do.

callout.title: Where the extra day should go
callout.body: If you have a fourth day, put it at Islands of Adventure rather than spreading it. It has the strongest ride list at the resort, its best attraction is excluded from every paid product so it needs a rope drop of its own, and it is the park where repeat rides on the coasters are most of the value.

sections.heading: The ticket decision that catches everybody
body: Universal Orlando sells base tickets, which admit you to one park per day, and park-to-park tickets, which let you move between parks on the same day. That sounds like a convenience upgrade. It is not, because the Hogwarts Express checks which one you hold.

The train runs between Hogsmeade at Islands of Adventure and Diagon Alley at Universal Studios Florida, and boarding it in either direction requires park-to-park. There is no upgrade sold at the platform. Families buy a base ticket to save money, arrive at the station on day two, and find out there. It is the most common expensive mistake at this resort.

What you keep on a base ticket is more than people expect: both halves of the Wizarding World are fully accessible on separate days, including Escape from Gringotts, Forbidden Journey, Hagrid's, the wand ceremony, the Butterbeer and the shops. What you lose is the train, which is an attraction with a different film in each direction rather than a transfer service.

So the decision is simple. If anyone in your party cares about Harry Potter, buy park-to-park and stop thinking about it. If nobody does, and you are on a short trip with young children, take the saving. The upgrade is priced per ticket rather than per day, so it gets cheaper per day the longer your trip is.

items: Decide park-to-park before you buy. It cannot be fixed at the Hogwarts Express platform.
Buy tickets in advance rather than at the gate. Multi-day tickets are cheaper per day and authorised resellers discount them.
Check whether Epic Universe is included in the ticket you are looking at, and on which days.
Match ticket days to park days honestly. An unused day on a ticket is money gone.
Link every ticket in the party to one Universal app account before you travel.

callout.title: The upgrade that pays for itself
callout.body: Park-to-park is priced as a flat addition to the ticket rather than per day. On a one-day visit it is at its most expensive relative to what it delivers; on a four-day ticket it is close to trivial per day and buys you the ability to change parks when a headliner goes down for weather. In a Florida summer that flexibility is worth the money on its own.

sections.heading: The height wall, and why it decides the trip
body: This is the section to read twice if you are travelling with children, because it is the difference between Universal and Disney that families feel most sharply.

Universal's thrill tier starts higher. Islands of Adventure's tallest requirement is 54 inches and its headline coasters cluster at 48, 51, 52 and 54. Universal Studios Florida tops out at 51. Epic Universe and Universal Studios Hollywood both top out at 48. Those are numbers a Disney park mostly does not use — Disney's tallest is 48 and the bulk of its list sits between 38 and 44.

The practical effect is that a child of a given height unlocks far less at Universal than at Disney. A 40-inch child at Magic Kingdom can ride a substantial share of the park. A 40-inch child at Islands of Adventure is looking at a much shorter list, and most of what their family came for is closed to them. There is no way to buy around this and no accommodation that helps.

The corresponding upside is that the height wall filters out most of what would have frightened them, with one exception worth knowing: Skull Island: Reign of Kong carries one of the lowest height minimums at Islands of Adventure and is one of the most intense environments at the resort. Do not treat the number as a proxy for intensity there.

Measure everybody at home, in the shoes they will wear, and be honest about it. Both resorts measure with a fixed stick and borderline guests get re-measured at every attraction until somebody says no. Building a trip around a child who is nearly tall enough is building it around a coin flip.

callout.title: If your youngest is under 40 inches
callout.body: Be realistic about what a Universal trip looks like. There is a good day at Universal Studios Florida between DreamWorks Land, the shows, E.T. Adventure and Minion Land, and a decent one at Islands of Adventure between Seuss Landing and Camp Jurassic. There is not a four-day trip. A family in that position gets more from Magic Kingdom, and this site would rather say so than sell you a week.

sections.heading: Where to stay, and why it is an Express decision
body: Universal Express Pass is a paid front-of-line product sold per person, per day, and it is included for every guest in the room, for the whole stay, at three of Universal Orlando's ten hotels: Loews Portofino Bay Hotel, Hard Rock Hotel and Loews Royal Pacific Resort. That is Universal's Premier tier. The other seven hotels do not carry it.

The reason this shapes the whole trip is arithmetic rather than luxury. Express is priced per person per day; the hotel premium is priced per room per night. A family of four multiplies one side by four and the other by one. On a busy date with two park days at the original parks, the Premier premium frequently comes in under what buying Express separately would cost — and the benefit is the Unlimited tier, and it covers arrival and departure days.

Every on-site Universal Orlando hotel, not just the Premier three, gets Early Park Admission: entry to a participating park an hour before the posted opening time. That is a genuinely valuable perk — an hour in Diagon Alley before the gates open is the most valuable early hour at the resort — and it is a completely different thing from Express. Confusing the two is how people book a value hotel expecting to skip lines.

One coverage point to confirm rather than assume: the hotel Express benefit has applied at Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure. Epic Universe opened in May 2025 on a separate campus with its own arrangements, which have moved since. Ask exactly which parks your room benefit covers at the point of booking.

items: Price Express Unlimited for your exact dates and party first. Then price the Premier hotel premium over your fallback hotel, multiplied by nights. Whichever is smaller wins.
Only count the people who would actually use Express. Not toddlers, not the adult who is sitting out the coasters.
Every on-site hotel gets Early Park Admission. Use it at Diagon Alley and nowhere else.
Several hotels connect to the two original parks by water taxi or a landscaped garden walkway, which is a real quality-of-life difference worth choosing a hotel over.
Confirm whether your room's Express benefit reaches Epic Universe before you rely on it.
Off-site is a legitimate choice at Universal in a way it is less so at Disney, because the parks are close to the main road corridor and there is no free airport shuttle to give up.

callout.title: The claim to disbelieve
callout.body: Express Pass is not a benefit of staying on site generally. It is a benefit of three named hotels. Anyone who tells you otherwise has read a summary rather than a booking page, and a family that believes it books the cheaper hotel and loses the entire value of the trade on day one.

sections.heading: The app, and setting it up before you go
body: The Universal app carries wait times, mobile food ordering, park hours, show schedules, any Virtual Line or timed-entry system that happens to be running, and the Power-Up Band game layer in SUPER NINTENDO WORLD. It is not optional in the way it once was.

Set it up at home. Download it, create the account, link every ticket in your party to that one account, and add a payment method. The in-park network is congested, and the morning you need the app working is the worst possible morning to be troubleshooting a login. This is a ten-minute job that repeatedly saves people an hour.

The two things worth checking in the app on arrival, before you plan anything: whether any attraction or land is running a Virtual Line or a timed entry, and the day's show times. At Epic Universe and Universal Studios Hollywood, SUPER NINTENDO WORLD entry has been managed since each park opened and the mechanism has changed more than once. Deal with that before you ride anything.

One thing the app will not do is book restaurants for you months in advance, because Universal does not work that way. There is no equivalent of Disney's sixty-day scramble, and the handful of full-service restaurants at these parks are bookable far closer to the date.

items: Download the Universal app and create the account at home, not in the security queue.
Link every ticket in the party to one account, including tickets bought separately by other members of the group.
Add a payment method for mobile food ordering.
On arrival, check for any Virtual Line or timed entry before you plan the morning.
Check show times when you arrive. Several of Universal's best attractions are shows that run on a schedule.

sections.heading: What a good first park day looks like
body: The shape of a Universal day is different from a Disney one because the tools are different. There is no morning booking scramble; instead the value is concentrated at the two ends of the day, and the middle is when you use whatever you paid for.

Be at the turnstiles thirty to forty-five minutes before the posted opening time, and earlier if you have Early Park Admission. Universal frequently opens the gates ahead of the posted hour and holds guests inside the first area. The first hour of a Universal day is worth more than any other hour, and at Islands of Adventure it is the only hour where Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure is a twenty-minute wait rather than a two-hour one.

Spend the middle of the day indoors and on whatever you have bought. This is the hour for Express Pass if you hold it, for a long lunch, for the shows, and for the air-conditioned rooms most people walk past. Florida afternoons on Universal's pavement are genuinely unpleasant and the parks are compact enough that there is nowhere to hide by accident.

Come back for the last two hours. Waits at the headliners fall sharply once families with young children leave, the single rider lines empty out completely, and several of these environments look their best after dark. The final hour is the second-best riding window of the day and almost nobody uses it deliberately.

items: Arrive 30 to 45 minutes before the posted opening, or before your Early Park Admission time.
Go straight to the one attraction that cannot be fixed later — Hagrid's at Islands of Adventure, Diagon Alley at Universal Studios Florida, SUPER NINTENDO WORLD entry at Epic Universe.
Ride standby in the first hour. Nothing you can buy beats an empty park.
Use the middle of the day for shows, food, and whatever pass you bought.
Use single rider lines from mid-afternoon onward, when they are at their most useful.
Stay for the last two hours. Waits fall, single rider queues empty, and the lands look better after dark.
Leave fifteen minutes before close from somewhere with a drink rather than joining the wave at the gate.

sections.heading: First-timer mistakes
body: Most of these are made before anyone arrives, which is what makes them expensive. Universal is a forgiving resort to visit and an unforgiving one to book.

The one that recurs most among people arriving from Disney is assuming the tools transfer. They do not. There is no morning booking window to win, the queue product works differently, the rider-switch equivalent keeps your party together in the queue, and the free single rider lines are a genuinely better deal than anything Disney offers. Reading the operator's own vocabulary is most of the work.

items: Buying a base ticket and discovering at the Hogsmeade station that the Hogwarts Express requires park-to-park.
Booking a non-Premier hotel expecting Express Pass. It is included at three hotels, not at on-site hotels generally.
Buying Express Pass in order to ride Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure. It has never been covered.
Not measuring the children before booking, and building a trip around a rider who is nearly tall enough.
Assuming you can walk or take the train to Epic Universe. It is a separate campus reached by bus, car or rideshare.
Ignoring the single rider lines. Twelve attractions across the two original parks have one, and almost nobody uses them properly.
Not checking the app for a Virtual Line or timed entry before planning the morning at Epic Universe or Hollywood.
Arriving at ten o'clock. The first hour is worth more than any product Universal sells.

callout.title: The five things to settle before you book anything
callout.body: Which resort. How many days. Base ticket or park-to-park. Premier hotel or not, after doing the Express arithmetic. And the height of the shortest person in your party, measured rather than estimated. Settle those five and the rest of a Universal trip is genuinely low-maintenance.

faqs.q: How many days do I need at Universal Orlando?
faqs.a: Three park days is the honest minimum now that Epic Universe exists. Two covers the two original parks at a rush and leaves Epic Universe out entirely. Four lets you repeat the headliners, which at Universal is more of the point than it is at Disney — the coasters reward second and third rides.

faqs.q: Do I need a park-to-park ticket?
faqs.a: You do if you want to ride the Hogwarts Express, which requires it in both directions and checks at the platform. Without it you can still see both halves of the Wizarding World on separate days, ride everything in each, and buy the wands and the Butterbeer. If anyone in your party is a Harry Potter fan, buy it; if not, the saving is legitimate.

faqs.q: Does Express Pass come with an on-site hotel?
faqs.a: Only at three of Universal Orlando's ten hotels — Loews Portofino Bay Hotel, Hard Rock Hotel and Loews Royal Pacific Resort, which are the Premier tier. Every on-site hotel gets Early Park Admission, which is a different and much cheaper benefit. Confusing the two is the most common booking mistake at this resort.

faqs.q: Is Universal good for young children?
faqs.a: Less so than Disney, and it is worth being honest about it. The height requirements are higher — Islands of Adventure tops out at 54 inches and its thrill tier clusters at 48 and above — and the gentle tier is thinner. There is a good day for a preschooler at Universal Studios Florida between DreamWorks Land, the shows and Minion Land. There is not a four-day trip.

faqs.q: Is Universal Orlando or Universal Studios Hollywood better?
faqs.a: Orlando, if you will only ever visit one. It is three parks, more rides, longer versions of several attractions Hollywood also has, and a hotel system with an Express tier. Hollywood has the Studio Tour on a real working lot, which Orlando cannot replicate, and it fits into one day inside a Los Angeles trip rather than requiring a trip of its own.

faqs.q: What time should I arrive at the park?
faqs.a: Thirty to forty-five minutes before the posted opening, and earlier if you have Early Park Admission from an on-site hotel. Universal frequently opens the gates ahead of the posted hour. The first hour is worth more than anything Universal sells, and at Islands of Adventure it is the only time Hagrid's is a short wait.

faqs.q: Do I need to book restaurants months in advance?
faqs.a: No. Universal has nothing resembling Disney's sixty-day dining scramble. There are only a handful of full-service restaurants across the parks and they are bookable much closer to the date, with walk-ups genuinely possible at several. CityWalk adds a large amount of capacity right outside the gates.

faqs.q: What is the one thing first-timers most often get wrong?
faqs.a: Buying Express Pass to ride Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure, which has been excluded from Express since it opened in 2019 and has no single rider line either. There is no product that shortens that queue. Rope drop, Early Park Admission, or the final hour before close are the only things that work.
